tagline: Down the Grand Staircase from the Sevier headwaters to Little Hollywood.
intro: US 89 turns south at the Bryce Canyon junction and follows the Sevier River up its valley, past Hatch near the headwaters, onto the Markagunt Plateau. Past the high point the road begins a long, steady descent through Long Valley and down the cliff bands of the Grand Staircase, Pink, Gray, White and Vermilion, to Kanab.

Long Valley was cattle country first. Ranchers came in 1862 to graze along the East Fork of the Virgin River, and the Mormon towns that took hold in the 1870s, Glendale and then Orderville, were settled by people from failed settlements on the Muddy River in Nevada.

moments.title: Hatch
moments.text: Settled in 1872 as Mammoth, the town in the Sevier valley near the river's headwaters later took the name of a pioneer citizen, Meltiar Hatch.

moments.title: Orderville
moments.text: Founded in 1875 to live the United Order, where no one held private property and families ate in community dining halls, men first, until the system ended in 1885.

moments.title: Kanab
moments.text: Locals call it Little Hollywood for the Westerns filmed around it, from Stagecoach in 1939 to The Outlaw Josey Wales in 1976.
